summary.text: Todd Achilles is an Independent candidate for U.S. Senate in Idaho. An Army veteran and technology executive who also teaches public policy, he was appointed to the Idaho House in 2024 and resigned in 2025 to run for the Senate. In his Ballotpedia survey, he lists his campaign priorities as stopping corruption in Congress, strengthening the middle class and protecting public lands.

paragraphs.text: Says he grew up on a family farm.

Earned a B.A. in economics and international relations from Claremont McKenna College, an M.B.A. and a master's in international studies from the University of Washington, and an M.P.A. from the University of California, Berkeley.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1992 to 1995; describes himself as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer.

Spent more than 20 years in senior roles at technology companies, according to his own account at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard and several startups; Ballotpedia lists his experience as including executive director of product management at T-Mobile, president at HTC, vice president/general manager at HP and CEO of Evoca.
Founded Veterans for Idaho Voters and has worked as a professor.

Was appointed to the Idaho House of Representatives (District 16B) in February 2024 to replace Rep. Colin Nash (D), and was elected to the seat in November 2024, defeating Jackie Davidson with 59.8% of the vote. He served on the Agricultural Affairs, Commerce and Human Resources, Ways and Means and State Affairs committees.
Resigned from the Idaho House in 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign; he lives in Boise with his family, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
